summary: Student-first machine candidate combining Harvard-wide guidance with FAS, HGSE, and HMS records. Course and unit rules remain controlling; the cited school and program policies are not generalized to every Harvard student.

dimensions.summary: Harvard-wide guidance and FAS guidance emphasize clear faculty communication of permitted AI use. Scope: university guidance plus FAS course communication, not a universal permission rule.

do: Check the course or assignment policy posted by the instructor.
dont: Do not treat a different Harvard school policy as your course rule.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed exam-specific student rule is included in this candidate; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
HGSE requires acknowledgement and documentation of permitted AI use. Scope: Harvard Graduate School of Education assignments, not all Harvard courses.

do: Follow the cited HGSE acknowledgement format when that policy applies.
dont: Do not extend HGSE disclosure wording to another Harvard unit without checking it.

dimensions.summary: Harvard-wide guidance restricts Level 2 and above confidential information to assessed and approved generative-AI tools; public tools are not the default path for Harvard work.

do: Check Harvard data classification and approved-tool status first.
dont: Do not enter confidential Harvard information into a public AI tool.

dimensions.summary: Harvard lists offered versions such as AI Sandbox, Gemini, Copilot Chat, ChatGPT Edu, and Firefly with stated data protections. Tool availability does not decide course or assessment permission.

do: Use only the Harvard-offered version and context covered by the cited classification.
dont: Do not infer academic-use permission from the approved-tools list.

dimensions.summary: HMS integrity guidance says AI tools cannot be authors and AI use in research should be transparent. Scope: Harvard Medical School guidance.

do: Disclose how AI was used when the HMS guidance applies.
dont: Do not list an AI tool as a paper author.
